artists.biography:
Spiritualized are a British space rock band formed in 1990 in Rugby, Warwickshire by Jason Pierce (who often goes by the alias J. Spaceman) after the demise of his previous band Spacemen 3. The membership of Spiritualized has changed from album to album, with Pierce — who writes, composes and sings all of the band's material — being the only constant member.

Spiritualized have released seven studio albums. The best known and most critically acclaimed of these is perhaps 1997's Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space, which NME magazine named as their Album of the Year.

perplexity.description:
Songs in A&E is the sixth studio album by English rock band Spiritualized, originally released in 2008. It marked the band's return after a five-year hiatus since 2003's Amazing Grace. The album's creation was deeply influenced by frontman Jason Pierce's near-death experience in 2005 due to a severe illness, which inspired its title referencing the Accident and Emergency ward where he was treated. Musically, the album continues Spiritualized's blend of space rock and neo-psychedelia, combining lush orchestration with raw, emotional rock elements, reflecting both vulnerability and intensity in its sound.

This album holds a significant place in Spiritualized's discography as a personal and artistic statement emerging from Pierce's health struggles. It features a more introspective and somber tone compared to previous works, yet retains the band's signature expansive and experimental rock style. The lead single "Soul on Fire" exemplifies this mix of heartfelt lyricism and rich musical layering. Upon release, Songs in A&E received positive critical acclaim, with some outlets ranking it among the best albums of 2008, highlighting its emotional depth and sonic ambition. It was released on Sanctuary Records in the UK and Fontana Records in the US, with Fat Possum Records handling some editions, underscoring its broad distribution and recognition within the rock genre.
